title: Gideon and the Wolf
premise: Gideon Winterbourne, a mercenary bound by oath to a god that has gone silent, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things: borrowed years, bottled names, second chances. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Gideon discovers she is the sold soul of a prince thought dead, and that his own forgotten past is written in her strange tongue. To reclaim her soul from the court beneath the mountain before the thirteenth moon turns, he must bargain with the guild's masked masters, confront the truth that he himself was once a ledger entry, and choose between restoring his stolen identity and saving hers. In the end, Gideon surrenders his own name to buy back the child's soul, becoming a man with no past but a future worth keeping.
about_author: Xanthe Villalobos is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obscure manuscripts before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about memory, debt, and the things people trade away, from a cluttered study overlooking a harbor town.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He audits the Vellum Guild's ledgers on a rain-slicked night, establishing the guild's eerie wares and his own hollow devotion to a silent god. A knock at the door interrupts him. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine, the sense that something is owed that no ledger records.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A mud-caked girl of eight stands in the storm, unafraid, and speaks a language that makes the guild's wards flare and the senior clerks go pale. She presses a copper coin into his hand stamped with a sigil Gideon somehow recognizes. Emotional beat: recognition without memory, dread blooming into protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Guildmistress Sarelle interrogates the child while Gideon eavesdrops; the girl's words are translated as 'thirteen moons' and 'beneath the mountain.' Sarelle orders the child locked away as an asset. Emotional beat: Gideon's first act of defiance, hiding the coin and lying to his employer.

chapters.title: The Silent God
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At his nightly vigil, Gideon prays to his sworn god and receives silence for the thousandth time, but tonight the silence feels watchful. He dreams of a mountain and a voice calling him by a name that is not Gideon Winterbourne. Emotional beat: loneliness curdling into suspicion about his own origins.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through her broken common tongue). The girl, Wren, reveals fragments: she remembers being someone else, a palace, a bargain made by adults, a price paid in her name. Emotional beat: innocence carrying an unbearable weight, the reader grasping the stakes before Gideon fully does.

chapters.title: The Broker of Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He seeks out Quill, a disgraced former guild broker living in exile, who examines the copper coin and goes white: it is court currency from beneath the mountain, minted for transactions involving souls. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, the thrill and terror of stepping off the ledger's page.

chapters.title: Sold Twice
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Quill explains that Wren's soul was sold once to the under-court and resold as collateral to the Vellum Guild itself — meaning Gideon's employers own a child's soul and intend to collect. Emotional beat: betrayal, the guild revealed as predator rather than neutral trader.

chapters.title: Breaking the Vault
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon steals Wren from the guildhouse during the moon-turning ceremony, using his mercenary skills for the first time against his own side. Sarelle catches him at the gate and lets him pass — with a warning that debts follow. Emotional beat: point of no return, fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Road Beneath a Dying Moon
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Gideon and Wren flee toward the mountain through country where the twelfth moon's light is failing. Wren teaches him words of her old language, and one phrase unlocks a flood of half-memories: a tower, a fire, a man signing a contract in blood. Emotional beat: tenderness between fugitives, grief surfacing.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A bridge-keeper demands payment in memories; Gideon sacrifices his memory of his mother's face to cross, testing how much of himself he is willing to spend. Wren weeps for what he lost though he cannot. Emotional beat: sacrifice foreshadowed, the theme of memory-as-currency made intimate.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Guild
chapters.summary: Sarelle's POV. The guild dispatches retrievers led by the enforcer Corvane, who carries a contract bearing Gideon's true signature — a signature Sarelle recognizes and fears. Emotional beat: antagonist depth, Sarelle's conflict between duty and dawning horror at what the guild has become.

chapters.title: Village of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The pair shelter in a village where everyone has sold years of their lives to survive; the elderly wear the faces of children. Wren restores one villager's stolen decade with a touch, revealing her soul's power. Emotional beat: hope, and the terrible realization that the under-court will want that power back.

chapters.title: Corvane Comes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Corvane ambushes them; in the fight, Gideon's old mercenary instincts surface with unsettling fluency, and Corvane taunts him: 'You signed with us long before you swore to your god.' Gideon spares him and flees shaken. Emotional beat: identity cracking open, violence as unwelcome homecoming.

chapters.title: The Name Under the Skin
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Quill arrives with proof: Gideon Winterbourne never existed before seven years ago. He is a constructed man, a ledger entry given flesh — possibly created by the guild, possibly by the silent god, as collateral or weapon. Emotional beat: existential vertigo, the question of whether a made self can be a real one.

chapters.title: Confronting the Silence
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon demands answers from his god at a ruined shrine and finally hears a reply: a single word in Wren's ancient language — 'Remember.' The god did not abandon him; it was waiting for him to be ready. Emotional beat: anguish turning to fierce purpose, faith rekindled through doubt.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Gideon and Wren's alternating POV. They enter the mountain through a door that only opens for souls already owed. Inside, the under-court glitters like a frozen feast, all its nobles wearing faces purchased from the living. Emotional beat: awe and revulsion, beauty as the mask of predation.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon bargains with the Pale Regent, who reveals the final truth: Gideon's own soul was the original collateral — Wren's sale was designed to lure him here and complete an old contract. Emotional beat: the trap closing, rage and clarity arriving together.

chapters.title: Sarelle's Choice
chapters.summary: Sarelle's POV. Sarelle arrives with Corvane, ostensibly to enforce the guild's claim, but having read the original contracts she instead burns the guild's copy before the Regent, voiding the resale and forcing a new bargain. Emotional beat: redemption through treachery, an antagonist choosing principle over survival.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. With the moon completing its turn overhead, the Regent offers terms: one soul for one soul. Gideon offers his own name and history — everything he is — to buy back Wren's. As the bargain seals, he begins to forget himself even while choosing it. Emotional beat: climax, self-annihilation as the purest form of love.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren wakes whole above ground but Gideon stands blank-eyed beside her, not knowing her name or his own. Using the language he learned on the road, she gives him back one memory — the phrase that means 'you chose this' — so he can begin again honestly. Emotional beat: grief braided with grace, identity rebuilt from a single true sentence.

chapters.title: A Man With No Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Months later, a nameless man works a small harbor town, mending nets and slowly writing new memories. Quill visits with news that the Vellum Guild has collapsed and Sarelle now guards its archives. Gideon does not remember any of it, and finds he minds less than he expected. Emotional beat: peace hard-won, freedom found in emptiness.

chapters.title: The First Word
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, restored to her princely birthright but choosing a simple life as Gideon's ward, teaches him the first word of the old language each morning. On the final page, he speaks a word neither taught him — the word for 'home' — hinting the silent god still keeps something of him safe. Emotional beat: quiet wonder, an ending that opens rather than closes.
